newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton, Hashimoto discuss trade disputes.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Hashimoto discuss trade disputes.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Sunday his Japanese counterpart had reaffirmed a desire to resolve outstanding trade disputes between the two economic giants.
Clinton was speaking after a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto at the APEC conference in Manila. Clinton said they had "spent a lot of time on trade in the meeting".

Asked by reporters if they made progress on trade issues, such as Japan's big trade surplus with the United States, Clinton said Hashimoto "reaffirmed his willingness to resolve any remaining disputes between us".
"If the economy keeps growing in Japan, that should help us reduce the trade imbalance," Clinton said.
Japan and the United States are at odds over a number of trade issues, including photographic film trade and the deregulation of Japan's insurance market.

The atmosphere was relaxed and friendly when the two leaders posed for pictures at the start of their talks on the sidelines of the annual conference of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

When Hashimoto was asked if he had any plans to surprise Clinton with a gift, like he did at their Tokyo summit in April by presenting the U.S. president with a saxophone, the Japanese leader said through an interpreter: "It's a diplomatic secret."
Clinton also held private meetings on Sunday with Chinese President Jiang Zemin and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
At the U.S.-Japan meeting, Hashimoto told Clinton that he welcomed the recent thaw in Sino-American relations, a senior Japanese government official told reporters.
"I am very happy that the U.S.-China summit was conducted in a good atmosphere," the senior Japanese official quoted Hashimoto as telling Clinton.
Clinton and Jiang agreed on Sunday on a framework for summit visits to each other's countries, marking a new warmth in their previously frosty relationship.

"It is not advisable to seek the isolation of China, and China is our important partner in this region," Hashimoto was quoted as saying. "I am happy that things are moving in the correct direction," Hashimoto added.

Hashimoto and Clinton did not discuss China's entry into the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in their meeting on Sunday, the Japanese official said. The subject of China's membership of the global trade body is expected to become one of the key issues in the APEC summit on Monday at Subic Bay north of Manila.
